newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian rebel sought for 50 murders killed - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian rebel sought for 50 murders killed - paper.

text.p: Algerian security forces shot dead a Moslem guerrilla leader sought for more than 50 murders, an Algerian newspaper said on Tuesday.
The French-language daily L'Authentique named the slain rebel as Brahim Kadi alias Kaalous who was killed on Monday in a gunbattle in La Glaciere, Algiers' southeastern suburb.
Another guerrilla, Redouane Chiha, was also killed in the shooting, said L'Authentique.
"Our bitter trial ends today. Kaalous will not act ruthlessly anymore," said an elderly man commenting on the militant killing, added the newspaper.
Moslem guerrillas are increasingly targeting civilians, including children and women, in the North African country where more than 250 non-combatants have been killed in the past six weeks.

About 60,000 people have died in Algerian violence opposing government forces and Moslem rebels since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election which radical Islamists were poised to win.
